answer: A system that clusters identities by their measured work patterns defeats clones because one operator cannot sustain many distinct timing patterns at once: each identity repeats three physical tasks daily for 30 days — crossing a dune on foot, tending a juniper cutting, and weighing a crystal grown from solution — logging start time, duration, and pauses for each task. Identities whose patterns match within 5 percent are grouped and lose half their weight together, so 100 fakes require 3,000 separate task-days.
